title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
This incident shows a failure in post-incident data handling for a deployed automated driving system. After a fatal crash involving Tesla's Autopilot, the company told a grieving family that key crash data was gone. A hacker later proved that every car keeps such data, and the data showed the system detected a hazard before the crash. The failure occurred not during driving but in the investigation and litigation phase, when stored vehicle data was claimed to be unavailable.

The failure mode is a false claim about data availability, not a model hallucination or an impersonation. It would have been caught by independent forensic access to the vehicle's storage, which is what the hacker performed. The reports do not establish that the missing-data claim was intentional rather than a technical or procedural error.
